text:
Eli: noticed sampleapp rerank crash in canary this morning, ValueError on reshape
Nora: how many items in the batch?
Eli: 3. Batcher merged them; response had mixed vector lengths (512 + 768) so `np.reshape(-1, 768)` failed
Sam: are we sure its not a client bug? which SDK version?
Eli: sherpa v0.8.1. Also saw a token refresh at roughly the same time that retried an in-flight request, seems to have created a near-duplicate which got merged
Nora: ah token refresh + retry + auto-batching could cause two similar requests to be combined and routed to different model variants -> mixed dims
Sam: short-term: add per-vector dim validation in the batcher and fall back to per-item calls if mismatch. Also surface the raw response in logs for debugging
Eli: implemented fallback locally, throughput drops but solves crash. opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sherpa/pull/58
Nora: long-term: SDK should provide preserve_order flag and idempotency dedupe to avoid merging retries. Also runtime should guarantee vec_dim invariant across model variants or document when it can change
DevEx Bot: incident-tag: dx-embed-dim; severity: low; owner: devex
auth-bot: token-refresh: 2025-09-03T08:12:01Z; retries: 1
Sam: I'll add an integration test that simulates auth latency: `AUTH_DELAY_MS=2000 make test-integration`
Eli: docs gap: onboarding guide never explicitly states vec_dim contract. I'll add a blurb and sampleapp test case
Nora: filing ENG-RUNTIME ticket to correlate model-variant fallback traces with mixed-dim responses
Eli: TL;DR: mixed-dim responses due to variant fallback + auth-retry merge -> SDK reshape crash. Temp fix = per-vector check + fallback; PR in flight.
